chapter: Kid Ory, Hampton, Ellington and Ben Webster
title: Norman Granz, George Wein and what jazz musicians were paid
summary: Mingus says promoters paid too little, citing his cheap first Jazz at the Philharmonic and Louis Armstrong's guarantee.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: What about (inaudible)? I mean, you've had a fair amount to say about the whole business of jazz. Has either one of them or both of them done something good in terms of the jazz musician?

(Inaudible), I never worked for him. When Billie Holiday demanded that he hire me because (inaudible), I did the first jazz philharmonic cheap because he's (inaudible). To work for nothing, because these two guys (inaudible) money. With George ______, they never paid enough money, man. Just before I got sick, I was able to find some agents who paid enough money. (Inaudible) ten dollars a concert. George ______ would have laughed if anybody asked for that kind of money.
That's interesting, because thre are classical musicians, and not only the very famous ones, the ones who are coming up, who get $10,000 a concert, but very few jazz people have ever done that.
The money went for (inaudible) corporation, when Louis was on salary. I forgot the salary that he was on.
I think it was $1,000 a week or something.
Yes. Every week he got a guarantee.
And Joe will tell you about how Louis was a big man in this corporation.
That's a big bell. You were saying Glacier said that Louis was a big man --
Yeah, it's all right, they can do that.
